code.originalText: Six-week review: symptoms, side effects, alcohol, sleep, and test results

text.paragraph: Six-week review: symptoms, side effects, alcohol, sleep, and test results. [S]

Mr. van Gogh returns six weeks after his first visit and two weeks after the sick visit for akathisia, when aripiprazole went back to 10 mg and propranolol was started. The restlessness eased within three days and has been gone for more than a week. The night-time voices have not returned on 10 mg. He sleeps six and a half to seven hours. He is painting again for a few hours most days, which he says matters more to him than anything. He takes naltrexone daily and now has one or two glasses of wine on most evenings; he notices that he wants a second glass less. His mood is better, and the thoughts of not waking up have stopped. He meets the care coordinator weekly and has seen the therapist twice. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-02; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 64.9 kg; blood pressure 120/76, pulse 76
No akathisia (Barnes global rating 0), rigidity, tremor, or abnormal movements
Brighter affect; organized; no psychotic features; insight good

First episode of psychosis with mood features: weeks of very little sleep, intense work and expansive plans, then acute confusion, hallucinations and suspiciousness with self-injury, and low mood since discharge. Diagnosis provisional; differential: bipolar I disorder with psychotic features, brief psychotic or schizophreniform disorder, alcohol withdrawal delirium or alcohol-induced psychotic disorder, and psychosis related to focal epilepsy. Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented first crisis
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented first crisis. Unspecified psychosis is coded because the cause is not yet established; the retrospective diagnoses stay in the claims.
Alcohol use disorder, moderate (heavy daily wine and anise spirits before the episode); synthetic modern episode linked to his documented heavy drinking
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented drinking and its retrospective interpretation.
Self-injury to the left ear during the acute confusional episode, without suicidal intent; wound healed after surgical care in hospital
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented injury; no detail of the injury is recorded.
Akathisia from aripiprazole, two weeks after the dose was increased to 15 mg; treated by returning to 10 mg and short-term propranolol; resolved
S — Synthetic medication side effect; not a historical claim.

list.item:
First episode of psychosis with mood features, provisional diagnosis (F29). Remission of psychotic symptoms on aripiprazole 10 mg. The brain MRI was normal, and the sleep-deprived EEG showed no epileptiform discharges; a normal EEG does not exclude focal epilepsy, but with no seizure-like events the team will not test further unless such events occur. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; the safety plan is current. [S]
Continue aripiprazole 10 mg daily.
Report any episodes of lost time, odd smells or tastes, or sudden fear, which would reopen the question of seizures.

Akathisia (G25.71). Resolved on the lower dose. [S]
Stop propranolol today.

Alcohol use disorder on naltrexone (F10.20). PEth down from 284 to 122 ng/mL; AST 41, ALT 37 and GGT 68 U/L, improving on naltrexone. [S]
Continue naltrexone and thiamine.
His own goal: no more than one glass of wine with dinner, and none on two days a week.
